title: Investigating the Anti-inflammatory Effect of Quinoline Derivative Loaded Nanoparticles
author: Medhat, El-Bana, et al.
materials: 1H NMR and 13C NMR analysis were used for the evaluation of the synthesized compound (NIQBD) 4 with 400 MHz and 100 MHz Bruker respectively. The FTIR spectrometer was carried out at Applied Nucleic acid research Center, Faculty of Science, Zagazig University using AlphaBruker ATR mode. The sample was prepared by using the KBr pellets technique. The Commercially available starting materials and solvents such as dimethyl formamide (DMF), and dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) were purchased from Sigma Aldrich and used as received without further purification. The key starting intermediate, 11-chloroneocryptolepine 1 was prepared according to our reported method [10]. Soluble starch was purchased from Doummar & Sons Co. Industrial City, Syria. Sodium hydroxide was purchased from El Nasr Pharmaceutical Chemicals, Egypt.

Methotrexate (50 mg) was purchased from MYLAN, USA. Homocystein standard (HPLC grade) was purchased from Sigma (St. Louis, USA). Other chemicals and reagents were of analytical grade (Sigma, St. Louis, USA).

steps.title: Characterize NIQBD by NMR and FTIR
steps.instruction: Perform 1H NMR at 400 MHz and 13C NMR at 100 MHz on the synthesized compound (NIQBD) using a Bruker spectrometer; prepare an FTIR sample by mixing the compound with KBr to form pellets and record spectra on an AlphaBruker ATR FTIR spectrometer.

steps.title: Acclimate and group experimental rats
steps.instruction: Obtain male Sprague‑Dawley rats weighing 140 ± 20 g, house them under controlled light and temperature with ad libitum standard diet and water; divide them into groups of eight rats each, following the NRC and NIH animal‑care guidelines.

steps.title: Prepare NIQBD‑loaded soluble starch nanoparticles
steps.instruction: Synthesize starch nanoparticles loaded with the desired amount of NIQBD (50 mg, 100 mg, or 200 mg) following the sequence below.

substeps.instruction: Disperse the chosen amount of NIQBD in 5 mL DMSO and ultrasonicate with a probe for 15 min at ambient temperature.
Gelatinize 0.2 g soluble starch in 50 mL deionized water containing 0.02 g NaOH by heating to 80 °C.
Add the NIQBD dispersion dropwise to the hot starch solution while stirring constantly for 5 min at 60 °C.
After gelatinization, sonicate the mixture for 30 min at room temperature.
Precipitate the NIQBD‑loaded starch nanoparticles by adding absolute ethanol and collect them by centrifugation (as described).
Place the pellet at –80 °C, then freeze‑dry at –80 °C for 24 h.
Grind the dried material to a fine powder; label the powders as StNPs‑1 (50 mg NIQBD), StNPs‑2 (100 mg NIQBD), StNPs‑3 (200 mg NIQBD). Prepare unloaded StNPs as a control.

steps.title: Make nanoparticle suspension for application
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.1 g of each dried nanoparticle powder, disperse in 10 mL deionized water, and sonicate for 15 min before use.

steps.title: Collect and homogenize lung and liver tissues
steps.instruction: Immediately excise lung and liver from each rat, rinse with ice‑cold saline, blot dry; homogenize left‑lung and liver portions in phosphate‑buffered saline to a 10 % (w/v) suspension, centrifuge at 4000 rpm for 15 min at 4 °C, and freeze the supernatants at –80 °C for later biochemical analysis. Retain the remaining tissue portions for histopathologic examination.

steps.title: Extract analytes from tissue supernatant
steps.instruction: Mix 400 µL of each frozen supernatant with 30 µL of 1.2 M trichloroacetic acid, incubate on ice for 30 min to precipitate protein, centrifuge at 3200 rpm at 4 °C for 20 min, and filter the clarified supernatant through a 0.45 µm PVDF membrane.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the resulting data with SPSS version 16, express results as mean ± standard error, and consider differences statistically significant at p < 0.05.
